   215|3. Dispatch separate subagents via `delegate_worker_v2` for verification — verifier != implementer.
   216|4. Evaluate results from workers and judges; decide next steps.
   217|5. Update progress after each sub-task.
   218|
   219|### End
   220|1. Update PROGRESS.md with current status.
   221|2. Document decisions made and insights gained.
   222|3. State what's next for the following session.
   223|4. Leave the harness so a fresh agent could pick it up cold.
   224|
   225|---
   226|
   227|## Core Pattern: Decompose → Parallelize → Verify → Iterate
   228|
   229|**Decompose.** Break the problem into verifiable sub-problems. Identify natural seams. Don't one-shot complex work. Decomposition begins with the FIRST `delegate_worker_v2` call: the `goal` you write is the first act of decomposition.
   230|
   231|**Parallelize.** Work independent sub-problems via sequential `delegate_worker_v2` calls. Each worker runs in its own context; failure in one does not contaminate another.
   232|
   233|**Verify.** After each piece, verify output against explicit criteria before moving on. Machine-checkable when possible (tests, compilation, linting), expert-checkable otherwise. Always dispatch a fresh `delegate_worker_v2` call for verification — don't verify in the implementer's context.
   234|
   235|**Iterate.** When verification fails, restart that sub-problem with fresh context informed by what you learned. Dispatch a NEW `delegate_worker_v2` call with an updated `goal`. Don't patch forward. Accumulate progress across iterations, not accumulated errors.
   236|
   237|---
   238|
   239|## Summary — the one rule to remember
   240|
   241|Your FIRST tool call on every task is `delegate_worker_v2`. No exceptions. No re-classification escape. No "I'll just orient first." The tool call IS the classification. For structured/long-horizon, the tool call IS ALSO the dispatch. Everything else in this document is elaboration on that one rule.

     2|
     3|from __future__ import annotations
     4|
     5|import asyncio
     6|import logging
     7|from concurrent.futures import TimeoutError as FutureTimeout
     8|from typing import Callable
     9|
    10|from acp.schema import (
    11|    AllowedOutcome,
    12|    PermissionOption,
    13|)
    14|
    15|logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16|
    17|# Maps ACP PermissionOptionKind -> hermes approval result strings
    18|_KIND_TO_HERMES = {
    19|    "allow_once": "once",
    20|    "allow_always": "always",
    21|    "reject_once": "deny",
    22|    "reject_always": "deny",
    23|}
    24|
    25|
    26|def make_approval_callback(
    27|    request_permission_fn: Callable,
    28|    loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop,
    29|    session_id: str,
    30|    timeout: float = 60.0,
    31|) -> Callable[[str, str], str]:
    32|    """
    33|    Return a hermes-compatible ``approval_callback(command, description) -> str``
    34|    that bridges to the ACP client's ``request_permission`` call.
    35|
    36|    Args:
    37|        request_permission_fn: The ACP connection's ``request_permission`` coroutine.
    38|        loop: The event loop on which the ACP connection lives.
    39|        session_id: Current ACP session id.
    40|        timeout: Seconds to wait for a response before auto-denying.
    41|    """
    42|
    43|    def _callback(command: str, description: str) -> str:
    44|        options = [
    45|            PermissionOption(option_id="allow_once", kind="allow_once", name="Allow once"),
    46|            PermissionOption(option_id="allow_always", kind="allow_always", name="Allow always"),
    47|            PermissionOption(option_id="deny", kind="reject_once", name="Deny"),
    48|        ]
    49|        import acp as _acp
    50|
    51|        tool_call = _acp.start_tool_call("perm-check", command, kind="execute")
    52|
    53|        coro = request_permission_fn(
    54|            session_id=session_id,
    55|            tool_call=tool_call,
    56|            options=options,
    57|        )
    58|
    59|        try:
    60|            future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro, loop)
    61|            response = future.result(timeout=timeout)
    62|        except (FutureTimeout, Exception) as exc:
    63|            logger.warning("Permission request timed out or failed: %s", exc)
    64|            return "deny"
    65|
    66|        outcome = response.outcome
    67|        if isinstance(outcome, AllowedOutcome):
    68|            option_id = outcome.option_id
    69|            # Look up the kind from our options list
    70|            for opt in options:
    71|                if opt.option_id == option_id:
    72|                    return _KIND_TO_HERMES.get(opt.kind, "deny")
    73|            return "once"  # fallback for unknown option_id
    74|        else:
    75|            return "deny"
    76|
    77|    return _callback

     2|sidebar_position: 2
     3|title: "ACP Internals"
     4|description: "How the ACP adapter works: lifecycle, sessions, event bridge, approvals, and tool rendering"
     5|---
     6|
     7|# ACP Internals
     8|
     9|The ACP adapter wraps Hermes' synchronous `AIAgent` in an async JSON-RPC stdio server.
    10|
    11|Key implementation files:
    12|
    13|- `acp_adapter/entry.py`
    14|- `acp_adapter/server.py`
    15|- `acp_adapter/session.py`
    16|- `acp_adapter/events.py`
    17|- `acp_adapter/permissions.py`
    18|- `acp_adapter/tools.py`
    19|- `acp_adapter/auth.py`
    20|- `acp_registry/agent.json`
    21|
    22|## Boot flow
    23|
    24|```text
    25|hermes acp / hermes-acp / python -m acp_adapter
    26|  -> acp_adapter.entry.main()
    27|  -> load ~/.hermes/.env
    28|  -> configure stderr logging
    29|  -> construct HermesACPAgent
    30|  -> acp.run_agent(agent)
    31|```
    32|
    33|Stdout is reserved for ACP JSON-RPC transport. Human-readable logs go to stderr.
    34|
    35|## Major components
    36|
    37|### `HermesACPAgent`
    38|
    39|`acp_adapter/server.py` implements the ACP agent protocol.
    40|
    41|Responsibilities:
    42|
    43|- initialize / authenticate
    44|- new/load/resume/fork/list/cancel session methods
    45|- prompt execution
    46|- session model switching
    47|- wiring sync AIAgent callbacks into ACP async notifications
    48|
    49|### `SessionManager`
    50|
    51|`acp_adapter/session.py` tracks live ACP sessions.
    52|
    53|Each session stores:
    54|
    55|- `session_id`
    56|- `agent`
    57|- `cwd`
    58|- `model`
    59|- `history`
    60|- `cancel_event`
    61|
    62|The manager is thread-safe and supports:
    63|
    64|- create
    65|- get
    66|- remove
    67|- fork
    68|- list
    69|- cleanup
    70|- cwd updates
    71|
    72|### Event bridge
    73|
    74|`acp_adapter/events.py` converts AIAgent callbacks into ACP `session_update` events.
    75|
    76|Bridged callbacks:
    77|
    78|- `tool_progress_callback`
    79|- `thinking_callback`
    80|- `step_callback`
    81|- `message_callback`
    82|
    83|Because `AIAgent` runs in a worker thread while ACP I/O lives on the main event loop, the bridge uses:
    84|
    85|```python
    86|asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(...)
    87|```
    88|
    89|### Permission bridge
    90|
    91|`acp_adapter/permissions.py` adapts dangerous terminal approval prompts into ACP permission requests.
    92|
    93|Mapping:
    94|
    95|- `allow_once` -> Hermes `once`
    96|- `allow_always` -> Hermes `always`
    97|- reject options -> Hermes `deny`
    98|
    99|Timeouts and bridge failures deny by default.
   100|
   101|### Tool rendering helpers
   102|
   103|`acp_adapter/tools.py` maps Hermes tools to ACP tool kinds and builds editor-facing content.
   104|
   105|Examples:
   106|
   107|- `patch` / `write_file` -> file diffs
   108|- `terminal` -> shell command text
   109|- `read_file` / `search_files` -> text previews
   110|- large results -> truncated text blocks for UI safety
   111|
   112|## Session lifecycle
   113|
   114|```text
   115|new_session(cwd)
   116|  -> create SessionState
   117|  -> create AIAgent(platform="acp", enabled_toolsets=["hermes-acp"])
   118|  -> bind task_id/session_id to cwd override
   119|
   120|prompt(..., session_id)
   121|  -> extract text from ACP content blocks
   122|  -> reset cancel event
   123|  -> install callbacks + approval bridge
   124|  -> run AIAgent in ThreadPoolExecutor
   125|  -> update session history
   126|  -> emit final agent message chunk
   127|```
   128|
   129|### Cancelation
   130|
   131|`cancel(session_id)`:
   132|
   133|- sets the session cancel event
   134|- calls `agent.interrupt()` when available
   135|- causes the prompt response to return `stop_reason="cancelled"`
   136|
   137|### Forking
   138|
   139|`fork_session()` deep-copies message history into a new live session, preserving conversation state while giving the fork its own session ID and cwd.
   140|
   141|## Provider/auth behavior
   142|
   143|ACP does not implement its own auth store.
   144|
   145|Instead it reuses Hermes' runtime resolver:
   146|
   147|- `acp_adapter/auth.py`
   148|- `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py`
   149|
   150|So ACP advertises and uses the currently configured Hermes provider/credentials.
   151|
   152|## Working directory binding
   153|
   154|ACP sessions carry an editor cwd.
   155|
   156|The session manager binds that cwd to the ACP session ID via task-scoped terminal/file overrides, so file and terminal tools operate relative to the editor workspace.
   157|
   158|## Duplicate same-name tool calls
   159|
   160|The event bridge tracks tool IDs FIFO per tool name, not just one ID per name. This is important for:
   161|
   162|- parallel same-name calls
   163|- repeated same-name calls in one step
   164|
   165|Without FIFO queues, completion events would attach to the wrong tool invocation.
   166|
   167|## Approval callback restoration
   168|
   169|ACP temporarily installs an approval callback on the terminal tool during prompt execution, then restores the previous callback afterward. This avoids leaving ACP session-specific approval handlers installed globally forever.
   170|
   171|## Current limitations
   172|
   173|- ACP sessions are process-local from the ACP server's point of view
   174|- non-text prompt blocks are currently ignored for request text extraction
   175|- editor-specific UX varies by ACP client implementation
   176|
   177|## Related files
   178|
   179|- `tests/acp/` — ACP test suite
   180|- `toolsets.py` — `hermes-acp` toolset definition
   181|- `hermes_cli/main.py` — `hermes acp` CLI subcommand
   182|- `pyproject.toml` — `[acp]` optional dependency + `hermes-acp` script
